name: Matrix Countdown Clock
author: Chuck Hergenroeder
description: Shows a live countdown to Christmas, New Year's Day or a date you choose on an LED matrix, held still in the center. The number and the text each have their own font, size and colour; under a day it switches to an HH:MM:SS timer or hours. Can also show your Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube handles with each site's logo, and a weather page with a sun, moon or wind symbol beside the temperature and wind, a show prep page with a QR code viewers scan to get the PulseMesh or Tune2 audio app, and your show times, each shown on its own, taking turns with the countdown for the seconds you choose. Weather comes from the internet weather service Open-Meteo (api.open-meteo.com, which receives this player's location rounded to about 1 km) or from your own WeatherFlow Tempest station on the local network. You choose; weather is off until you turn it on.

privacy.summary: Draws a countdown and your social handles on a matrix here. With Weather on, it gets weather from Open-Meteo (sending your location, rounded) or hears your Tempest station on your network.

sends.to: http://the FPP player you set as FPP Host (this device by default)
sends.what: requests for the list of overlay models and to turn the chosen model on and off
sends.why: to draw the countdown on a matrix attached to that player

sends.what: this player's latitude and longitude, rounded to about 1 km, every 15 minutes
sends.why: to get the current temperature, wind and whether it is day, only with Weather on and Open-Meteo chosen

systemChanges.what: runs a background program whenever FPP is running, which draws the countdown frames
its background program listens on 127.0.0.1:32330, reachable only from this device; FPP's web server passes requests to it
with Weather on, listens for UDP broadcasts on port 50222 (shared with other listeners) to read a Tempest station; sends nothing

privacy.other: Its API is served through FPP's web server, so anyone who can open this player's FPP pages can change its settings and turn its output on or off, the same as FPP itself. Its FPP commands (countdown on/off, set target) do the same from anything that can run FPP commands, including the scheduler, MQTT and other FPP players. It switches the overlay model you choose on and off and writes pixels into that model's overlay buffer. It writes an activity log (logs/plugin-fpp-matrixcountdown.log). Its settings (config/plugin.fpp-matrixcountdown.json) and a weather location you type in (plugindata/fpp-matrixcountdown/location.json) stay after uninstall.
